ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Microbial coverage after source control

A young adult has a peritonsillar abscess drained. The clinician selects antibiotics to address organisms normally found in the oropharynx, including mixed flora. Which coverage is most relevant when choosing an empiric regimen according to local guidance?

  1. Streptococci and oral anaerobes
  2. Streptococci without anaerobic coverage in every setting
  3. Enteric gram-negative rods and enterococci
  4. Pseudomonas species and atypical mycobacteria
  5. Mycoplasma and Chlamydia species
Answer and explanation

Streptococci and oral anaerobes

Peritonsillar infections commonly involve streptococci and oral anaerobic organisms; local resistance and allergy influence the regimen.

Option explanations

Streptococci and oral anaerobes: Peritonsillar infections commonly involve streptococci and oral anaerobic organisms; local resistance and allergy influence the regimen.

Streptococci without anaerobic coverage in every setting: Mixed oral flora may be relevant; regimen choice must consider local guidance rather than assuming anaerobes never matter.

Enteric gram-negative rods and enterococci: These are not the principal microbial groups in a typical peritonsillar abscess.

Pseudomonas species and atypical mycobacteria: This spectrum is not routinely needed for uncomplicated infection of this site.

Mycoplasma and Chlamydia species: These atypical respiratory organisms are not the main pathogens in a suppurative peritonsillar collection.
